---
title: "Performance & Reliability"
---

IrisPipe separates **merge-gating regression tests** from long-running capacity benchmarks:

- **k6 Benchmark:** API/runtime latency, 1k / 10k / 100k data-volume behavior, failure semantics, and PostgreSQL-to-H2 coverage.
- **Backend K6 Checks:** 10 regression suites against a real Spring Boot backend.
- **k6 Deep Volume Benchmark:** scheduled/manual retained capacity snapshots.
- **Full RDBMS Matrix:** six source-specific workflows covering H2, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, and Oracle. A full run is 6 sources x 6 destinations x JOB/CHUNK x 1M/10M/50M = **216 cases**.

## What the Benchmark Measures

The data-volume benchmark exercises real Spring Batch + JDBC execution and validates both throughput and data correctness:

1. Regular PR/main gate: H2-to-H2 JOB/CHUNK at 1k / 10k / 100k.
2. Failure semantics: a duplicate key on the final row proves the JOB vs CHUNK rollback boundary.
3. Cross-database correctness: destination row count must equal the expected row count; `COMPLETED` alone is not accepted as a pass.
4. Full matrix: every source can target every destination across H2 / PostgreSQL / MySQL / MariaDB / SQL Server / Oracle.
5. Capacity ladder: 1M / 10M / 50M for both JOB and CHUNK (baseline, sustained throughput, capacity stress).

All numbers are repeatable GitHub-hosted-runner regression benchmarks, **not production-capacity claims**.

---

## Benchmark Dataset Schema

Every full/deep case migrates the same simple logical row shape so database-engine behavior, JDBC reading, writing, batching, and transaction boundaries remain the variables under test.

```text
benchmark_source
  id    PRIMARY KEY    values 1..N
  name                 "row-<id>"

source query
  SELECT id, name FROM benchmark_source ORDER BY id

destination
  benchmark_dest       same logical columns, empty before a success run
```

| Database | `id` physical type | `name` physical type | DB-side source seed method |
|---|---|---|---|
| H2 | `INT PRIMARY KEY` | `VARCHAR(255)` | `SYSTEM_RANGE(1, N)` |
| PostgreSQL | `INT PRIMARY KEY` | `VARCHAR(255)` | `generate_series(1, N)` |
| MySQL | `INT PRIMARY KEY` | `VARCHAR(255)` | set-based Cartesian product of decimal digit sets, filtered to `N` |
| MariaDB | `INT PRIMARY KEY` | `VARCHAR(255)` | set-based Cartesian product of decimal digit sets, filtered to `N` |
| SQL Server | `INT PRIMARY KEY` | `VARCHAR(255)` | digit CTE Cartesian product + `TOP (N)` + `ROW_NUMBER()` |
| Oracle | `NUMBER(10) PRIMARY KEY` | `VARCHAR2(255)` | bounded 10k `CONNECT BY` block x `ceil(N/10k)`, filtered to `N` |

The payload is deterministic: row `123` is `{id: 123, name: "row-123"}`. Source data is generated with set-based SQL **inside the database before timing starts**; k6 does not submit N individual inserts. Same-engine external cases use separate `benchmark_source` and `benchmark_dest` tables in one engine instance; cross-engine cases use separate source and destination containers.

## Fetch vs Batch

IrisPipe exposes two independent tuning concepts even though the current benchmark profiles intentionally set them to the same value for a controlled comparison:

- `fetchSize`: source-side JDBC reader fetch window/hint. It affects read round trips, driver buffering, and memory behavior. It is **not** a transaction boundary.
- `batchSize`: destination-side writer batch/chunk size. In CHUNK atomic mode it also defines the commit boundary; in JOB atomic mode batches are still written incrementally but the whole job shares one destination transaction.

| CI profile | Source `fetchSize` | Destination `batchSize` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Regular PR/main benchmark | 1,000 | 1,000 |
| Deep/full benchmark | 5,000 | 5,000 |

The raw full/deep tables display both values separately. Older retained snapshots were produced before `fetch_size` was persisted in the JSON report; those harness versions explicitly configured `fetchSize = batchSize`, so the renderer can recover the historical Fetch value without guessing.

---

## JOB vs CHUNK: Transaction Boundary

The same `batchSize` has different transaction semantics:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph JOB["JOB / 50M rows"]
    J1["JDBC batches: 5,000 rows"] --> J2["1 destination transaction"] --> J3["Failure: rollback all 50M"]
  end
  subgraph CHUNK["CHUNK / 50M rows"]
    C1["10,000 chunks x 5,000 rows"] --> C2["10,000 independent commits"] --> C3["Failure: rollback only failing chunk"]
  end
```

| Source rows | CHUNK transaction groups @ 5,000 | JOB transaction groups |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1M | 200 | 1 |
| 10M | 2,000 | 1 |
| 50M | 10,000 | 1 |

The regular 10k failure test makes the trade-off observable. With a duplicate key on the final row and a 1,000-row batch, **JOB** rolls back all migrated rows and leaves only the pre-existing conflict row (**1 row**). **CHUNK** preserves the first nine committed chunks (**9,000 rows**) and rolls back only the failing tenth chunk, leaving **9,001 rows** including the pre-existing conflict.

---

## Benchmark Timing Boundary

Reported `duration_ms` / `rows_per_second` intentionally measure **IrisPipe migration execution**, not environment setup.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["DB/container startup"] --> B["Source seed"] --> C["Backend startup"] --> D["Pipeline config"] --> E["START TIMER"] --> F["POST /sync-pipeline<br/>Spring Batch + JDBC + commits"] --> G["STOP TIMER"] --> H["Destination COUNT verification"] --> I["Publish report"]
```

**Included:** the synchronous `/api/v1/sync-pipeline` call from immediately before the request until the completed/failed response returns.

**Excluded:** database/container startup, source-data generation, backend startup/readiness, pipeline-config creation, post-run destination `COUNT(*)`, artifact aggregation, and Pages deployment.

This is why smaller cases can show lower rows/s: fixed Spring Batch / JDBC / transaction startup cost is amortized over fewer rows.

---

## Throughput Chart Reading

The chart uses **X = source row count on a log scale** and **Y = measured rows/second**. Each source database is a tab, each destination is a curve, and JOB/CHUNK are separate tabs. This keeps the load level on the independent axis and makes throughput saturation or degradation visible as the dataset grows.

Each circle is an actual 1M / 10M / 50M measurement. The line uses shape-preserving cubic interpolation only as a visual guide through those points; it does not create or imply additional benchmark samples.

## CI / Benchmark Triggering

Long-running 50M tests never block normal PR merges or ordinary `main` Pages deployment.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  PR["PR / main push"] --> G["Unit tests + regular k6 gates"]
  G --> P["Deploy Quarto using retained benchmark JSON"]

  T["tag: benchmark-full-*"] --> H2["Source H2 / 36 cases"]
  T --> PG["Source PostgreSQL / 36 cases"]
  T --> MY["Source MySQL / 36 cases"]
  T --> MA["Source MariaDB / 36 cases"]
  T --> MS["Source SQL Server / 36 cases"]
  T --> OR["Source Oracle / 36 cases"]

  M["Manual: Full RDBMS Benchmark - All Sources"] --> H2
  M --> PG
  M --> MY
  M --> MA
  M --> MS
  M --> OR

  H2 --> R["Serial merge into retained deep-performance-results.json"]
  PG --> R
  MY --> R
  MA --> R
  MS --> R
  OR --> R
  R --> D["repository_dispatch to GitHub Pages"]
```

A source-specific tag such as `benchmark-postgres-*` triggers only that source workflow; `benchmark-full-*` triggers all six source workflows.

The retained result file uses a merge key of `(db_pair, atomic_level, mode, row_count, fetch_size, batch_size)`. A normal merge to `main` **does not regenerate or clear deep results**, and a source-specific benchmark update replaces only the cases it actually measured.

---

## Benchmark Methodology

1. `mvn package` runs backend unit tests before benchmark execution.
2. Regular PR/main gates stay bounded; 10M+ capacity work is tag/manual/scheduled only.
3. Full matrix jobs use `fetchSize=5,000`, `batchSize=5,000`, and validate 1M / 10M / 50M; each source workflow runs 36 cases with `max-parallel=4`.
4. Source seed happens before the migration timer; k6 does not insert the benchmark dataset row-by-row.
5. External destination row counts are verified after the timer and must equal the expected count.
6. Benchmark snapshots are merged into retained history instead of replacing unrelated source/destination results; legacy 100K/20M measurements remain retained even though they are no longer part of the active ladder.
